method: Fixed independent confirmation: opening 21 and all 23 remaining replies. Exactly the previous GNUbg leader and the published XG leader, selected before the new run. 4096 new trials per move in 128 independent 32-trial batches. Shared dice within each pair; no seed overlaps with the earlier experiment or other diagnostic positions. Same Short/deep policy, engine, rules and endpoints; no optional stopping. Primary contrast is previous GNUbg choice minus XG choice. New trials are analyzed separately from the selection sample. Two-sided paired Student-t intervals at 95%, plus Bonferroni simultaneous 95% coverage for 24 fixed contrasts. This tests sampling noise in this pipeline, not the correctness of XG or the neural evaluator alone.

reference.note: Sum of reported marginal half-widths, not a paired XG confidence interval or a familywise bound; shared-dice covariance is unavailable.

limitations: Independent confirmation of 24 previously selected pairs, not a general-strength benchmark or a full reranking of all legal moves.
Familywise intervals use paired batch means and a Bonferroni correction over 24 fixed contrasts; their coverage relies on the usual Student-t approximation.
Persistent means the previous choice remains preferred within this fixed GNUbg pipeline, beyond estimated sampling noise. It does not prove XG is correct or isolate a neural-network defect.
Truncation, checker/cube policies, move filters, neural evaluation, cube modeling and reference error can all contribute. XG enables beavers; our rollouts do not.
XG marginal intervals cannot recover the paired uncertainty of its move gap. The published opening book remains unchanged by this two-move diagnostic.
